knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Slope of the Tangent to a Parametric Curve at a Given Point

question.:question/problem:
For the parametric curve 

$$
x=3 \sec^{2} {t},\,y=5 \csc^{3} {t},\,0<t<\frac{\pi}{2},
$$

calculate the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $t=\frac{\pi}{6}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
x'(t)=6 \tan {t} \sec^{2} {t},\,y'(t)=- 15 \cot {t} \csc^{3} {t}.
$$

 

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{\left(- 15 \cot {t} \csc^{3} {t}\right)}{\left(6 \tan {t} \sec^{2} {t}\right)} \\  & =- 15 \cot {t} \csc^{3} {t}\left(\frac{\cos^{2} {t} \cot {t}}{6}\right) \\  & =- \frac{5}{2}\,\cos^{2} {t} \cot^{2} {t} \csc^{3} {t} \\  & =- \frac{5}{2}\left(\frac{1}{\sin^{3} {t}}\right)\left(\frac{\cos^{2} {t}}{\sin^{2} {t}}\right)\cos^{2} {t} \\  & =- \frac{5 \cos^{4} {t}}{2 \sin^{5} {t}} \\  & =- \frac{5 \cot^{4} {t} \csc {t}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, when $t=\frac{\pi}{6},$ the slope of the tangent to the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =- \frac{5 \cot^{4} {\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)} \csc {\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-15\cdot \left(2\right)\cdot \left(\sqrt{3}\right)^{4}}{6} \\  & =-45.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
For the parametric curve 

$$
x=\frac{1}{6 \sqrt{t}},\,y=\frac{e^{t}}{4 t},\,0<t<\infty,
$$

calculate the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $t=5.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
x'(t)=- \frac{1}{12 t^{\frac{3}{2}}},\,y'(t)=\frac{4 t e^{t} - 4 e^{t}}{16 t^{2}}=\frac{\left(t - 1\right) e^{t}}{4 t^{2}}.
$$

 

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{\left(t - 1\right) e^{t}}{4 t^{2}}\cdot \left(- 12 t^{\frac{3}{2}}\right) \\  & =- \frac{3 \left(t - 1\right) e^{t}}{\sqrt{t}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, when $t=5,$ the slope of the tangent to the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =- \frac{3 \left(\left(5\right) - 1\right) e^{\left(5\right)}}{\sqrt{\left(5\right)}} \\  & =\frac{- 12 e^{5}}{\sqrt{5}} \\  & =- \frac{12 \sqrt{5} e^{5}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

calculate the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $t=5.$

We will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
x'(t)=- \frac{1}{10 t^{\frac{3}{2}}},\,y'(t)=\frac{t e^{t} - e^{t}}{t^{2}}=\frac{\left(t - 1\right) e^{t}}{t^{2}}.
$$

 

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{\left(t - 1\right) e^{t}}{t^{2}}\cdot \left(- 10 t^{\frac{3}{2}}\right) \\  & =- \frac{10 \left(t - 1\right) e^{t}}{\sqrt{t}}.\end{aligned}

Therefore, when $t=5,$ the slope of the tangent to the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =- \frac{10 \left(\left(5\right) - 1\right) e^{\left(5\right)}}{\sqrt{\left(5\right)}} \\  & =\frac{- 40 e^{5}}{\sqrt{5}} \\  & =- 8 \sqrt{5} e^{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
For the parametric curve 

$$
x=e^{\frac{3}{t}},\,y=\frac{5}{\sqrt{t^{2} + 1}},\,0<t<\infty,
$$

calculate the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $t=4.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
x'(t)=- \frac{3 e^{\frac{3}{t}}}{t^{2}},\,y'(t)=- \frac{5 t}{\left(t^{2} + 1\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}}.
$$

 

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{\left(- \frac{5 t}{\left(t^{2} + 1\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}}\right)}{\left(- \frac{3 e^{\frac{3}{t}}}{t^{2}}\right)} \\  & =\frac{5 t^{3} e^{- \frac{3}{t}}}{3 \left(t^{2} + 1\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, when $t=4,$ the slope of the tangent to the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{5 \left(4\right)^{3} e^{- \frac{3}{\left(4\right)}}}{3 \left(\left(4\right)^{2} + 1\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}} \\  & =\frac{320}{51 \sqrt{17} e^{\frac{3}{4}}} \\  & =\frac{320 \sqrt{17}}{867 e^{\frac{3}{4}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
For the parametric curve 

$$
x=e^{\frac{6}{t}},\,y=\frac{1}{\sqrt{t^{2} - 1}},\,1<t<\infty,
$$

calculate the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $t=3.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
x'(t)=- \frac{6 e^{\frac{6}{t}}}{t^{2}},\,y'(t)=- \frac{t}{\left(t^{2} - 1\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}}.
$$

 

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{\left(- \frac{t}{\left(t^{2} - 1\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}}\right)}{\left(- \frac{6 e^{\frac{6}{t}}}{t^{2}}\right)} \\  & =\frac{t^{3} e^{- \frac{6}{t}}}{6 \left(t^{2} - 1\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, when $t=3,$ the slope of the tangent to the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{\left(3\right)^{3} e^{- \frac{6}{\left(3\right)}}}{6 \left(\left(3\right)^{2} - 1\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}} \\  & =\frac{27}{96 \sqrt{2} e^{2}} \\  & =\frac{9 \sqrt{2}}{64 e^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

x'(t)=- \frac{2 e^{\frac{2}{t}}}{t^{2}},\,y'(t)=- \frac{6 t}{\left(t^{2} + 3\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}}.

\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{\left(- \frac{6 t}{\left(t^{2} + 3\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}}\right)}{\left(- \frac{2 e^{\frac{2}{t}}}{t^{2}}\right)} \\  & =\frac{3 t^{3} e^{- \frac{2}{t}}}{\left(t^{2} + 3\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}}.\end{aligned}

question.:question/problem:
For the parametric curve 

$$
x=5 \sqrt{\sin{\left(e^{t} \right)}},\,y=6 \cot{\left(e^{t} \right)},\,-\infty<t<1,
$$

calculate the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $t=\ln{\left(\frac{\pi}{6} \right)}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x'(t)&=\frac{5}{2 \sqrt{\sin{\left(e^{t} \right)}}}\cdot \cos{\left(e^{t} \right)}\cdot e^{t}\\ &= \frac{5 e^{t} \cos{\left(e^{t} \right)}}{2 \sqrt{\sin{\left(e^{t} \right)}}},\\ y'(t)&=- 6 e^{t} \csc^{2}{\left(e^{t} \right)}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{\left(- 6 e^{t} \csc^{2}{\left(e^{t} \right)}\right)}{\left(\frac{5 e^{t} \cos{\left(e^{t} \right)}}{2 \sqrt{\sin{\left(e^{t} \right)}}}\right)} \\  & =\frac{- 12 \sqrt{\sin{\left(e^{t} \right)}}}{5 \sin^{2}{\left(e^{t} \right)} \cos{\left(e^{t} \right)}} \\  & =- \frac{12}{5 \sin^{\frac{3}{2}}{\left(e^{t} \right)} \cos{\left(e^{t} \right)}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, when $t=\ln{\left(\frac{\pi}{6} \right)},$ the slope of the tangent to the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =- \frac{12}{5 \sin^{\frac{3}{2}}{\left(e^{\left(\ln{\left(\frac{\pi}{6} \right)}\right)} \right)} \cos{\left(e^{\left(\ln{\left(\frac{\pi}{6} \right)}\right)} \right)}} \\  & =\frac{-12}{5\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{3/2}\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)} \\  & =- \frac{16 \sqrt{6}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
x=5 \sqrt{\sin{\left(e^{t} \right)}},\,y=2 \cot{\left(e^{t} \right)},\,-\infty<t<1,
$$

calculate the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $t=\ln{\left(\frac{5 \pi}{6} \right)}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x'(t)&=\frac{5}{2 \sqrt{\sin{\left(e^{t} \right)}}}\cdot \cos{\left(e^{t} \right)}\cdot e^{t}\\ &= \frac{5 e^{t} \cos{\left(e^{t} \right)}}{2 \sqrt{\sin{\left(e^{t} \right)}}},\\ y'(t)&=- 2 e^{t} \csc^{2}{\left(e^{t} \right)}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{\left(- 2 e^{t} \csc^{2}{\left(e^{t} \right)}\right)}{\left(\frac{5 e^{t} \cos{\left(e^{t} \right)}}{2 \sqrt{\sin{\left(e^{t} \right)}}}\right)} \\  & =\frac{- 4 \sqrt{\sin{\left(e^{t} \right)}}}{5 \sin^{2}{\left(e^{t} \right)} \cos{\left(e^{t} \right)}} \\  & =- \frac{4}{5 \sin^{\frac{3}{2}}{\left(e^{t} \right)} \cos{\left(e^{t} \right)}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, when $t=\ln{\left(\frac{5 \pi}{6} \right)},$ the slope of the tangent to the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =- \frac{4}{5 \sin^{\frac{3}{2}}{\left(e^{\left(\ln{\left(\frac{5 \pi}{6} \right)}\right)} \right)} \cos{\left(e^{\left(\ln{\left(\frac{5 \pi}{6} \right)}\right)} \right)}} \\  & =\frac{-4}{5\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{3/2}\left(- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)} \\  & =\frac{16 \sqrt{6}}{15}.\end{aligned}
$$
